$comment: ★★ A LINKED OBJECT'S IMAGE REQUESTS LAND IN THE HEADER (P69 round 4, D-LK-COFF-READER-SKIPPED-EVERY-LINKER-DIRECTIVE). The archive's one member is cl 19.44's `/c /O2 /MD /GS-` build of six `#pragma comment(linker, ...)` lines and `int dss_header_member(void) { return 0; }` -- its `.drectve`: `/HEAP:0x200000,0x10000 /VERSION:3.5 /SUBSYSTEM:WINDOWS,6.02 /ENTRY:mainCRTStartup /BASE:0x200000000 /ALIGN:0x2000`. main.c reads each field back from its own image: the heap reserve and commit (2), the image version 3.5 (3), the GUI subsystem (4), its version 6.02 (5) and the operating-system version link.exe sets with it (6), the 8 KiB section alignment (7) and every section's address on it (8). The image is a GUI one and still exits 42: its startup calls `main`, the C runtime's console startup the member names. ✔MEASURED 2026-10-07 (`.orchestrators/p69/work/xa/r4fix/fix.log`): the same main.c built by cl and linked against this archive runs to 42 under link.exe 14.44; lld-link 19.1.5 refuses the member (`/HEAP:`, `/VERSION:`, `/BASE:` and `/ALIGN:` are 'not allowed in .drectve'), and acceptance is the union's. The preferred base is not read back: the image is DYNAMIC_BASE, so the loader places it where it chooses (the header field is pinned by `CoffDirectiveImageRequests.TheHeaderRequestsLandWithLinkExesPrecedence`). The member's `/ENTRY:mainCRTStartup` is the startup the image has anyway, and a member the archive search pulls names no entry (`examples/c/pe_foreign_directive_entry_from_an_archive_member_warned`), so it changes nothing and says nothing.
